name: The Fir of Ashuku Hachiman Shrine

location.address: Ashuku Hachiman Jinja, Toyosaka-cho Ashuku, Higashi-Hiroshima, Hiroshima Prefecture

access: Free. Small rural shrine, presumed open, no restriction found.
transport: No train or bus stop nearby; reachable by car in rural Toyosaka-cho.
verify_notes: Report ID 53641, Ministry of Environment giant-tree register (kyoju.biodic.go.jp), surveyed 2000: girth 3.40m, health good ('良好'), no age band recorded ('不明'). This is the ONLY source found for this specific tree despite three separate searches (general web, a shrine-directory/mapion pattern search that worked for sibling trees hgh_008/009/019, and the city's own Toyosaka-cho cultural-properties page at city.higashihiroshima.lg.jp, which lists only the Hongu Hachiman Shrine building and the Renkyo-ji Asunaro as designated properties, nothing at Ashuku). Context only, not corroboration: Hongu Hachiman Shrine (already published as hgh_015/016/017, ~5km away) was historically the tutelary shrine for five constituent villages, one of which is Ashuku/Asshuku (安宿), per higashihiroshima-kanko.jp's own page on Hongu Hachiman -- this explains why a local Hachiman branch shrine carrying the Ashuku name would plausibly exist here, but it is not a source for the tree itself. No coordinate given by the register at all; the pin used is the Nominatim centroid for the 豊栄町安宿 hamlet (quarter-level, not shrine-level), roughly 3km from the already-published black pine at Tokuzen-ji (hgh_019) and roughly 5km from the Uneyama Shrine cluster (hgh_010-014), so it sits inside the same rural Toyosaka-cho car-reachable area as those trees rather than forming a walkable cluster with them. Health was recorded good with no dieback in the 2000 survey (26 years old now); no news, removal record or any other mention found either way. Girth recorded per the standing rule even though no age can be derived from it without a documented growth rate for Abies firma in this soil.
